$schema: Aykon Ventures · Typography System · Edition 02 · Final

cinzel.name: Cinzel
cinzel.usage: the logo wordmark, display caps, section titles, vertical names — CAPS ONLY
cinzel.notes: Roman inscriptional caps — the lettering of monuments, banks and maisons. Placeholder for the wordmark until the custom Route C cut lands from the type designer.

cormorant.name: Cormorant
cormorant.usage: headlines, deks, pull-statements — sentence case, the voice of every document
cormorant.notes: High-contrast serif — jewellery-house elegance without the fashion-house froth

inter.name: Inter
inter.usage: all body copy, UI text, captions, decks, screens — never the wordmark or headlines
inter.notes: A quiet, neutral grotesque that steps back so the serifs lead

amiri.name: Amiri
amiri.usage: ALL Arabic text — wordmark (ايكون فينتشرز), headlines, body — co-equal with Latin
amiri.notes: Classical Naskh — heritage register. Designed beside the Latin from sketch one. Never translated by tool — bilingual copy lead writes Arabic native.

jetbrains_mono.name: JetBrains Mono
jetbrains_mono.usage: monospace for figures, terms, eyebrows, labels, prices, stakes, RERA partner names
jetbrains_mono.notes: The 'plain about money' principle made typographic — figures line up, proof reads as proof

pairing_rules: Cinzel names. Cormorant writes. Inter reads. Mono carries the money.
Serif leads, sans supports. Never invert.
Sentence case always — except Cinzel display caps and mono eyebrows, which are caps by nature.
Arabic ايكون فينتشرز gets its own line — never squeeze Amiri to Latin x-height; give diacritics vertical room.
Prices, stakes, terms and labels in JetBrains Mono.
Weights restrained: Cinzel 600-700; Cormorant 400-600; Inter 400-680. No ultra-thin, no black.
